title: Workmanship Guarantee Conditions
content:
# Conditions of the Work Order: The Workmanship Guarantee

The Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service stands behind its own workmanship for the months your service level sets, counted from the day the piece was handed back.

1. **The period.** A piece is taken back under the guarantee only when the handling date has not passed the guarantee period in whole calendar months counted from the date the piece was handed back to the customer. The date the piece was handed back is the one standing on the work order; the customer's recollection of when they collected it does not move that date.

2. **How the months are counted.** Guarantee months are counted as whole calendar months from the day of delivery, and where the anniversary day does not exist in the closing month the boundary falls on the last day of that month. The boundary day itself is within the guarantee: a piece brought in on the boundary day has not passed the period, and a piece brought in the day after it has.

3. **What rework costs.** Rework inside the guarantee is carried out without charge at the levels that carry it free, and one order goes back to the bench no more times than the level allows. The times an order has gone back are counted over the whole life of that work order, from intake to the handling date.

4. **What the guarantee answers for.** The guarantee answers for the chain's own workmanship and not for fresh damage, ordinary wear or work another workshop has since done on the piece, and where the bench finds one of those the rework is priced as new work.

5. **Where the allowance is used up.** Where the rework limit is reached the desk does not send the piece back again under the guarantee, and the customer is offered a fresh estimate instead.

## Boundary cases on hypothetical dates

Take a hypothetical order at a level whose guarantee runs 6 whole months, with the piece handed back on the 14th of a month. The boundary falls on the 14th of the sixth month following. Brought in on that boundary day, the piece has not passed the period and is within the guarantee; brought in on the following day, it has passed it.

Take a second hypothetical order at the same level, with the piece handed back on the 31st of a month, where the sixth month following has only 30 days. The anniversary day does not exist in that closing month, so the boundary falls on its last day, the 30th. Brought in on that 30th, the piece is within the guarantee; brought in on the 1st of the next month, it is not.
